display.text:
# frozen_string_literal: true

module RuboCop
  module Cop
    module Style
      # Check for chained `dig` calls that can be collapsed into a single `dig`.
      #
      # @safety
      #   This cop is unsafe because it cannot be guaranteed that the receiver
      #   is an `Enumerable` or does not have a nonstandard implementation
      #   of `dig`.
      #
      # @example
      #   # bad
      #   x.dig(:foo).dig(:bar).dig(:baz)
      #   x.dig(:foo, :bar).dig(:baz)
      #   x.dig(:foo, :bar)&.dig(:baz)
      #
      #   # good
      #   x.dig(:foo, :bar, :baz)
      #
      #   # good - `dig`s cannot be combined
      #   x.dig(:foo).bar.dig(:baz)
      #
      class DigChain < Base
        extend AutoCorrector
        include RangeHelp
        include CommentsHelp
        include DigHelp

        MSG = 'Use `%<replacement>s` instead of chaining.'
        RESTRICT_ON_SEND = %i[dig].freeze

        def on_send(node)
          inspect_chain(node)
        end
        alias on_csend on_send

        private

        # Walk up the method chain while the receiver is `dig` with arguments.
        def inspect_chain(node)
          already_ignored = false
          current_ignored_nodes = ignored_nodes
          ignored_index = 0
          while ignored_index < current_ignored_nodes.size
            if current_ignored_nodes[ignored_index].equal?(node)
              already_ignored = true
              break
            end
            ignored_index += 1
          end
          return if already_ignored

          node_location = node.loc
          send_dot = node_location.dot
          return unless send_dot
          return unless dig?(node)

          collected_arguments = node.arguments.dup
          chain_end_pos = node.source_range.end_pos
          chain_begin_pos = nil
          receiver_node = node.receiver

          while receiver_node
            if dig?(receiver_node)
              receiver_location = receiver_node.loc
              receiver_dot = receiver_location.dot
              if receiver_dot
                chain_begin_pos = receiver_dot.begin_pos + 1
              else
                chain_begin_pos = 0
              end
              receiver_arguments = receiver_node.arguments
              collected_arguments.unshift(*receiver_arguments)
              ignore_node(receiver_node)
              receiver_node = receiver_node.receiver
            else
              break
            end
          end

          return unless chain_begin_pos

          forwarded_args_index = nil
          argument_index = 0
          arguments_count = collected_arguments.size
          while argument_index < arguments_count
            argument = collected_arguments[argument_index]
            if argument.forwarded_args_type?
              forwarded_args_index = argument_index
              break
            end
            argument_index += 1
          end

          if forwarded_args_index
            remaining_index = arguments_count - 1
            if remaining_index.positive?
              if forwarded_args_index < remaining_index
                return
              end
            end
          end

          offense_range = range_between(chain_begin_pos, chain_end_pos)

          argument_sources = []
          source_index = 0
          while source_index < arguments_count
            argument_sources << collected_arguments[source_index].source
            source_index += 1
          end
          argument_source = argument_sources.join(', ')
          replacement = "dig(#{argument_source})"
          offense_message = format(MSG, replacement: replacement)
          related_comments = comments_in_range(node).to_a

          add_offense(offense_range, message: offense_message) do |corrector|
            corrector.replace(offense_range, replacement)
            comment_index = related_comments.size - 1
            while comment_index >= 0
              comment = related_comments[comment_index]
              corrector.insert_before(node, "#{comment.source}\n")
              comment_index -= 1
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

      expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo, :bar)::dig(:baz, :quux)
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(:foo, :bar, :baz, :quux)` instead of chaining.
      RUBY

      expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo, :bar, :baz, :quux)
      RUBY
    end

    it 'registers an offense and corrects with splat' do
      expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo).dig(*names).dig(:bar)
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(:foo, *names, :bar)` instead of chaining.
      RUBY

      expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo, *names, :bar)
      RUBY
    end

    it 'registers an offense and corrects when split over multiple lines' do
      expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo)
          ^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(:foo, :bar, :baz)` instead of chaining.
         .dig(:bar)
         .dig(:baz)
      RUBY

      expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo, :bar, :baz)
      RUBY
    end

    it 'registers an offense and corrects when split over multiple lines with comments' do
      expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
        x.dig(:foo) # comment 1
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(:foo, :bar, :baz)` instead of chaining.
         .dig(:bar) # comment 2
         .dig(:baz) # comment 3
      RUBY

      expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
        # comment 1
        # comment 2
        x.dig(:foo, :bar, :baz) # comment 3
      RUBY
    end

    context '`...` argument forwarding' do
      it 'registers an offense and corrects with forwarded args' do
        expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
          def foo(...)
            x.dig(:foo).dig(...)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(:foo, ...)` instead of chaining.
          end
        RUBY

        expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
          def foo(...)
            x.dig(:foo, ...)
          end
        RUBY
      end

      it 'does not register an offense when combining would add a syntax error' do
        expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
          def foo(...)
            x.dig(...).dig(:foo)
            x.dig(...).dig(...)
          end
        RUBY
      end

      context 'Ruby >= 3.1', :ruby31 do
        it 'does not register an offense when `dig` is given a forwarded anonymous block' do
          expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
            def foo(&)
              x.dig(&).dig(:foo)
            end
          RUBY
        end
      end

      context 'Ruby >= 3.2', :ruby32 do
        it 'registers an offense and corrects with forwarded anonymous splat' do
          expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
            def foo(*)
              x.dig(*).dig(*)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Use `dig(*, *)` instead of chaining.
            end
          RUBY

          expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
            def foo(*)
              x.dig(*, *)
            end
          RUBY
        end

        it 'does not register an offense with forwarded anonymous kwsplat' do
          expect_no_offenses(<<~RUBY)
            def foo(**)
              x.dig(**).dig(:foo)
            end
          RUBY
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `lib/rubocop/cop/style/dig_chain.rb:70`: the chain start position was computed as `receiver_dot.begin_pos + 1`, which only skipped one character. For a safe-navigation receiver (`&.`, a 2-character token), the range began inside the `&.`, leaving a stray `&` and producing `hoge&dig(:a, :b)`. Using `receiver_dot.source.size` correctly skips the whole dot token (also handles `::`).

Verified:
- `spec/rubocop/cop/style/dig_chain_spec.rb`, `single_argument_dig_spec.rb`, and `cli/autocorrect_spec.rb` all pass (174 examples, 0 failures)
- End-to-end check: `hoge&.dig(:a)&.dig(:b)` now autocorrects to `hoge&.dig(:a, :b)`
